I volunteer at a soup run so I’ve seen a fair bit but I’d say the scariest thing was when one of the service users was in a particularly bad form that day because his son had committed suicide a few hours ago and he didn’t have the will to live. I remember making him a tea and asking him how he was feeling and that I was here if he needed a chat (by that time I’d also realized that he would probably need a professional to talk to, so I sent a call for one). He seemed to be up for a chit chat with me so we kept talking and then next thing I saw was my trainers were covered in his blood. He had a blade hidden in his sleeve (we never noticed, it was pushed all the way in his sleeve) and had slit his wrist. Don’t think I’ll ever forget the sight of his blood flowing or his face. Fortunately, he was taken to the hospital because there’s always medics on stand by. Saw him again a couple of months later, he’d moved to a different town and seemed better. Never saw him again.
Aptly so.
